findings.body: The new `promotedBy: "agent"` value is accepted globally, but this consistency check runs only when `source` is `agent_self_edit`. An otherwise valid fact with `source: "tool_result"`, `verificationStatus: "human_approved"`, and `promotion.promotedBy: "agent"` passes this guard, is stored by `RuntimeMemoryStore.appendFact`, and appears in ordinary recall as human-approved. This is a newly accepted contradiction, not preserved historical human lineage. Enforce approval consistency whenever the promoter identifies an agent action, and cover this combination in the regression test.
findings.title: Reject human-approved facts whose promoter is the agent

findings.body: The candidate guard rejects human approval but still accepts `agent_self_edit` records claiming `verified` or `deterministic_rule`. Adding a finite `proposedAt` to such a contradictory accepted-fact record causes `isRuntimeMemoryTemporalFact` to reject it, then `sanitizeQueryableFactForStore` falls through to this candidate guard and stores it with the claimed status while stripping its promotion. It remains readable through `getFactById` and explicit status queries, defeating the required rejection before mutation. Apply the self-edit approval invariant to the candidate fallback, or reject malformed accepted-fact records before falling back, and add regression coverage beyond `human_approved`.
findings.title: Prevent candidate fallback from bypassing self-edit approval checks

overall_explanation: The handlers generate agent provenance, preserve historical human lineage, and leave persistence retired. However, two schema paths still accept contradictory approval records. This was a read-only source review; tests were not run, as requested.
